The historical map room

Read the map’s date and maker.

These documents include Indigenous knowledge, colonial cartography and government surveys. Their names, classifications and boundaries reflect particular times and purposes. They do not establish present Indigenous territories. A surviving copy is identified as a copy. Date filters follow the catalogue’s publication or copy date; an earlier design is explained in the record.

Featured maps

1836 · Historical scholarship

Map of the Indian tribes of North America, about 1600 A.D. along the Atlantic, & about 1800 A.D. westwardly

Albert Gallatin; American Antiquarian Society

Gallatin assembled this map for an American Antiquarian Society publication in 1836. Its title distinguishes eastern depictions around 1600 from western depictions around 1800. Compare its historical naming and classifications with later maps; its labels do not define current communities or borders.

Albert Gallatin; Pendleton’s Lithography. David Rumsey Historical Map Collection, list no.3388.001. Digital image © Cartography Associates. CC BY-NC-SA 2.0 ↗.

1873 · Federal reservation administration

Proposed Nez Perce reservation in the Wallowa Valley

Office of Indian Affairs, U.S. Department of the Interior (archive attribution; individual drafter unidentified)

This federal map outlines a proposed reservation in northeastern Oregon. Its title explicitly names Nez Perce people and the Wallowa Valley; red lines, rivers and survey divisions explain the proposed tract. Read it alongside the government's 1873 order. The map records an administrative proposal rather than the full Nez Perce homeland or present boundaries.

Office of Indian Affairs, Department of the Interior; NARA, RG 75, E107, Executive Order File, Box 2, Wallowa Valley. Digital image: University of Idaho Library, Archival Idaho Photograph Collection, NARA16DC2. Public Domain Mark 1.0 ↗.

Linguistic Stocks of American Indians North of Mexico.
